meta.title: Primordial Paradox music recipes, Konami gothic rock and metal family
meta.citation_note: Every recipe cites source ids from knowledge/music-styles/konami.md section 13. Full titles, URLs and read dates live there, not here, because this directory is scanned by the project's clean-room gate.
meta.chip: NES 2A03 (2 pulse, triangle, noise, DPCM) plus Konami VRC6 (2 pulse, saw)
meta.reference_rule: study only; no melody transcribed, ripped, traced or decompiled

measured_anchors.note: all from the corpus statistics file cited as K22 in the study; tempo in that file is normalised and is not used

recipes.name: Gallop cell, long plus two shorts
recipes.when_to_use: The main riff of any stage or boss cue in this style, in place of straight eighths.

params.channel_low_end: triangle root on the long note only
params.channel_hat: noise on the two short notes

forbidden: triplet or shuffle feel inside the cell
putting the kick on a short note instead of the long one
running the cell below 110 bpm where the shorts merge into the long note

recipes.name: Reverse gallop answer
recipes.when_to_use: The answering half of a two bar riff, so the second bar pushes into the next downbeat rather than restarting on it.

params.placement: bars 2 and 4 of a 4 bar group

forbidden: using it as the opening cell, because it reads as a pickup and the hook then has no downbeat
mixing it inside the same bar as the standard gallop

recipes.name: Driving eighth bass under a sixteenth riff
recipes.when_to_use: Whenever the melody is on sixteenths and the low end needs to stay legible; the default bass of the whole style.

params.motion: root only, one pitch per eighth
params.octave_jumps: only at the last eighth of a 4 bar group
params.contrast_target: melody at 0.62 to 0.89 beats per note against bass at 0.5 beats per note

forbidden: walking a new bass note every eighth when the harmony changes only once per bar
bass above MIDI 58, which collides with the inner voice median of 61.5

recipes.name: Harmonic minor riff frame
recipes.when_to_use: The scale skeleton of a stage or boss riff when the cue must sound old and gothic rather than merely sad.

params.leading_tone: raised seventh, 11 semitones above the tonic
params.augmented_second: between flat 6 and raised 7, allowed once per 2 bars
params.cadence_chord: major dominant from the raised seventh

forbidden: the augmented second in a title hook
natural seventh and raised seventh in the same bar
two augmented seconds in one phrase

recipes.name: Raised seventh cadence
recipes.when_to_use: End of every 4 bar group where the loop must feel finished but still push on.

params.penultimate: V or V7 built on the raised seventh
params.melody_at_cadence: approach the tonic by semitone from below or by the raised seventh

forbidden: a minor v at the cadence, which flattens the style into modal rock
more than one cadence per 4 bars

recipes.name: Flat two Neapolitan stab
recipes.when_to_use: Crypt, castle hall, boss entrance, anywhere the cue must sound older and stranger than the key allows.

params.chord: major triad a semitone above the tonic
params.length: one beat or one sixteenth stab
params.voice_leading: bass steps up a semitone to the tonic after the stab
params.melody: hold the tonic over the stab for the tritone against the chord root

forbidden: the flat two chord in the same bar as the raised seventh
two flat two stabs in a 4 bar group
using it in a stage clear or ending cue

recipes.name: Flat five dominant
recipes.when_to_use: The dominant before the tonic in a stage theme that wants harmonic bite without jazz vocabulary.

params.chord: dominant triad with a flat five added
params.melody_note: flat five above the bass for the tritone, resolved by semitone
params.example_reading: the measured Mad Forest intro and verse opens on a V with a flat five

forbidden: resolving the flat five upward by whole tone
stacking a seventh on top of the flat five in a stage cue
more than one flat five dominant per 4 bars

recipes.name: Diminished hinge chord
recipes.when_to_use: Mid riff, at the weakest metric point of the bar, to make the ear expect a resolution the riff then delays.

params.chord: diminished triad or half diminished seventh on the second degree
params.position: the and of 2 or the and of 3
params.resolution: up a fourth to the dominant or down a semitone to a chord tone

forbidden: diminished chord on a downbeat
a diminished seventh held longer than an eighth
two different diminished chords in one bar

recipes.name: Second inversion climb
recipes.when_to_use: The Mad Forest path: a rising harmonic sequence for boss and crypt cues where the harmony, not the melody, carries the identity.

params.bass_motion: step up by semitone or tone for 3 or 4 chords
params.chords: second inversion shapes with the third or fifth in the bass
params.hinge: one diminished chord in the middle of the climb
params.melody_behaviour: stay on chord tones, tension under 25
params.example_reading: the measured Mad Forest intro and verse climbs through ii42, III42 and IV42 with a mixture before V42 and i

forbidden: climbing more than 5 chords without a landing
a melodic counterline that also climbs, which doubles the motion and kills it
using the climb on a 4 bar stage clear

recipes.name: Chromatic bass walk
recipes.when_to_use: The transition bar between two 4 bar groups, when the cue needs to move to a new harmony without a cadence.

params.direction: up to the next chord root
params.chord_above: keep a common tone in the upper voice if possible
params.channel: triangle, or vrc6_saw when the chip allows

forbidden: chromatic walks in both directions inside one 4 bar group
a chromatic walk under a melody that is also chromatic

recipes.name: Organ arpeggio at frame rate
recipes.when_to_use: Title, crypt and boss intro, where the harmony must be a wall rather than a progression.

params.channel: pulse1 plus vrc6_p1 alternating notes to raise the repeat rate to 30 Hz

forbidden: arpeggiating at less than 15 notes per second, which sounds like an arpeggio rather than a chord
two channels playing the same arpeggio in phase, which produces one louder voice with no width
arpeggio above the melody

recipes.name: Held organ chord on VRC6
recipes.when_to_use: Only on VRC6 cues: a sustained chord under a riff, the string imitation the extra channels were used for.

params.duty_mode: 100 percent for a flat organ tone, or 12.5 percent for strings
params.voicing: root and fifth only, third supplied by the arpeggio

forbidden: three held notes on two channels at once
held organ in a five channel arrangement, where it takes the channel the riff needs
vibrato on a held organ chord

recipes.name: Saw bass riff
recipes.when_to_use: VRC6 stage themes: the bass line is the riff, not just the roots.

params.motion: riff root plus one passing note per bar
params.octave: one below the melody median of MIDI 71

forbidden: accumulator rate above 42, which distorts
saw and triangle doubling the same line for a whole cue
saw bass above MIDI 55

recipes.name: Saw and triangle split octaves
recipes.when_to_use: The first 4 bars only, as an intro weight device before one channel drops out.

params.drop: triangle out at bar 5, or saw out if the cue needs a thinner middle

forbidden: running the split for a whole cue
splitting at the octave above, which puts the saw in the inner voice register

recipes.name: Two pulse register crossing
recipes.when_to_use: The Vampire Killer path: the lead and the second guitar trade the same cell and cross registers.

params.crossing: voice_b plays one octave up on its second trade, then back
params.measured_reference: 16 bar loop with the squares crossing registers in the published commentary

forbidden: both pulses on the same duty
crossing more than twice in a 16 bar loop
register crossing on a held note rather than on the cell

recipes.name: Call and response bars
recipes.when_to_use: A section stage theme of 15 to 45 bars, where one riff must cover the whole length.
forbidden: response in a different key
a response that is longer than the call, which unbalances the 4 bar group

recipes.name: Dotted eighth echo voice
recipes.when_to_use: Title and crypt cues on a five channel arrangement, to fake space without losing a voice to a pad.

params.channel: pulse2 when the riff is not using it
params.duty: different from the lead by one step

forbidden: an echo on a gallop cell, where the delay lands on the short notes and smears them
echo volume above 45 percent

recipes.name: Fast sixteenth fill, two beats
recipes.when_to_use: Every 8 bars, or at the end of a phrase group, to turn the corner into the next riff.

params.kit_double: snare noise sixteenths under the last beat
params.end: DPCM tom or kick on the downbeat after the fill

forbidden: fills longer than 3 beats
a fill in every 4 bar group
a fill on the same channel as a held note, which forces a cut

recipes.name: Descending harmonic minor run
recipes.when_to_use: Phrase end in a boss cue, when the melody has to fall away rather than cadence.

params.harmonic_support: diminished hinge on the second degree at the midpoint

forbidden: the run on a title hook
two runs in one 8 bar group
the run in parallel thirds on both pulses

recipes.name: Stop time break
recipes.when_to_use: Boss transition, or the last bar before a loop restarts, to reset the ear.

params.content: DPCM kick on beats 1 and 3 only, everything else silent
params.return: full riff plus organ arpeggio on the downbeat after

forbidden: a stop time break in the first 4 bars of a cue
silence longer than 1 bar
a break before a half cadence, which double stalls the loop

recipes.name: Boss tempo lift plus minor second pedal
recipes.when_to_use: The boss version of a stage cue, when the two cues should sound related but not the same.

params.pedal: tonic in the bass on eighths
params.pedal_neighbour: flat second above the tonic as a sixteenth neighbour once per bar
params.riff: same cell as the stage theme, register up an octave
params.drum: kick doubled on the second sixteenth of each beat
params.metre: keep 4/4 unless the boss cue is the odd metre exception

forbidden: the flat second neighbour in every bar, which becomes the melody
a boss cue that shares the stage theme's full melody, which erases the difference
tempo lift above 155 bpm on a five channel arrangement

recipes.name: Four bar riff to hook, one change on repeat three
recipes.when_to_use: The standard construction for any stage hook in this style.

params.leap: one leap of a fourth or more at a fixed position in every repetition
params.wobble: neighbour tone oscillation around one pitch, the measured most common interval pair

forbidden: changing the identifying two bars on the third repetition
more than one variation per 7.4 s pass
ending the fourth bar on a full authentic cadence every pass

recipes.name: Half cadence loop ending
recipes.when_to_use: Default ending for any loop, because the measured repertoire ends open far more often than closed.

params.share_reference: half cadence 15.4 percent of measured phrases against authentic 3.4 percent
params.melody: end on the second degree or the fifth, not the tonic
params.last_bar: one beat of riff then the dominant held

forbidden: a tonic final chord on a stage loop unless the cue is a one shot
ending on the tonic in the melody while the chord is the dominant, which fights the loop

recipes.name: Transposition ladder
recipes.when_to_use: Boss escalation or the last 8 bars of a long stage theme, when the riff must climb without new material.

params.step: up a fourth or up a minor third
params.return: back to the tonic for the final 2 bars
params.adjustment: keep the riff inside a 45 semitone window

forbidden: more than two ladder steps
transposing the bass and the melody by different intervals
a ladder in a 15 bar loop that has not yet stated the riff three times

recipes.name: Run and gun march kit
recipes.when_to_use: Contra style stage cues: straight 4/4, snare backbeat, bass eighths, melody in the middle register.

params.snare: noise mid rate on beats 2 and 4
params.kick: beats 1 and 3 plus the and of 3
params.melody: steps and neighbour tones, leap share under 40 percent

forbidden: swing on the hats
snare on beat 3 only, which is the Castlevania pattern not the Contra one
fills longer than one beat in a 17 bar loop

recipes.name: Odd metre arpeggio wall
recipes.when_to_use: The one boss cue per game that is allowed to break 4/4, following the Gradius boss lineage.

params.content: rising arpeggio on the pulses, pedal bass on every beat
params.mode_colour: Lydian raised fourth for the space or dread colour
params.drums: kick on 1 and 4, snare on the last beat of the bar

forbidden: odd metre more than once per game
odd metre with a gallop cell, which loses the pulse
an odd metre cue under 8 bars, which cannot establish the metre

recipes.name: Stage clear fanfare under 4 bars
recipes.when_to_use: Stage clear, all clear, item get, and the short one shots, which in the measured set are 1 to 4 bars.

params.channels: pulse1 lead, pulse2 harmony, noise roll on the last beat
params.ending: tonic, held, with the noise decay as the tail

forbidden: a stage clear longer than 4 bars
a half cadence here, because these cues are the one place the style closes
drum kit beyond one roll

recipes.name: Duty change inside a note
recipes.when_to_use: Human touch on any held note longer than a quarter, once per cue.

params.applies_to: notes of a quarter or longer
params.avoid: the hook note and the cadence note

forbidden: two duty changes inside one note
a duty change on a sixteenth, which is inaudible and costs engine time

recipes.name: One frame push on short notes
recipes.when_to_use: Any gallop or sixteenth riff that sounds quantised after rendering.

params.applies_to: the short notes of the gallop cell only
params.grid: 60 Hz frame, so the smallest legal step is 16.7 ms

forbidden: pushing the downbeat, which destroys the lock with the kick
pushing beyond one frame, which reads as a mistake rather than as drive

recipes.name: Layered loop with 1, 2 and 4 bar periods
recipes.when_to_use: Any stage loop of 15 bars or more, so the piece never sounds identical across two passes.

params.variation: drop one of the three layers for 2 bars at bar 9, then restore it
params.reference: short units recombined with nested loops across voices

forbidden: all layers on the same period, which produces an audibly identical repeat
dropping the melody layer, which the ear hears as a gap rather than as variety
a loop longer than 16 bars without a new element at bar 9
